title: Initial Archivist migration grill
goal: Shape the standalone Archivist repo and decide how to migrate from the EPP generated browser toward a Vite-based local document app.

resolved_decisions.summary: Archivist should be a general local document-workbench, not an EPP-only app.
The EPP manual should remain the first serious workspace/proving corpus because it is complex and immediately useful.
Local copies for coworkers should be supported for EPP work, but the architecture should not trap future content inside EPP assumptions.
The app may sit beside selected EPP workflow concepts, especially recommended edits and review acceleration.
Markdown bundles remain canonical for v1, with approved changes writing back through review gates.
Archivist needs git-like document history: latest approved content is the normal view, while humans and models can inspect what changed, when, and why across long time horizons.
Use a hybrid history model: real Git for durable file history and diffs, plus an Archivist audit ledger that links proposals, approvals, rationale, exports, and review metadata to commit hashes.
Use a small bundled EPP seed workspace for the first scaffold, while preserving a manifest shape that can later open a full external EPP workspace.
Archivist v1 targets desktop-only local use; mobile layout and mobile smoke validation are out of scope.
The port target includes the old EPP Markdown/browser functionality and local chat/manual-agent workflow, not only the initial Vite scaffold.
The full EPP content corpus should live in the Archivist repo as a standalone workspace, not only as a few seed files.
Workbooks should be a first-class artifact family. Appendix A / HVA is the first workbook implementation, not a one-off exception.
Approved workbook state should live in structured sidecar JSON files linked to the parent document and workbook ID, while Markdown remains the explanatory wrapper and definition source.
The HVA prototype should start by proving the service-backed workbook sidecar state boundary before polishing the HVA UI.
The first HVA UI should edit draft workbook sidecar state directly while keeping approved sidecar writes locked behind future review/apply.
The old EPP manual browser UI/layout is the parity baseline. The current app gap is that Appendix A is not yet visible as a normal document because the app still uses the seed document list.
Restore the full EPP browser shell and navigation before continuing deeper HVA workbook UI polish.
Use a compatibility renderer first for Markdown, CFR, compliance, and artifact output, then promote high-value surfaces into React components after the browser shell is stable.
Fold service-backed workspace and document reads into SG-0013 instead of keeping SG-0002 as a separate prerequisite.
Render document views live from canonical source inside the app; reserve pre-rendering for export, print, review snapshots, or disposable caches.
Define a provider-neutral local agent interface, with an LM Studio/OpenAI-compatible local endpoint as the first adapter.
Keep manual edits and model proposals separate at input time, but converge accepted output into the same review, Git history, and audit ledger path.
Create one Git commit by default for each accepted model proposal or approved manual-draft batch; add review-session batching later only if needed.

readiness_call.reason: All current grill questions are resolved. SG-0013 is ready to build next.
